Rashi on Pesachim 78a:10:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - הא דקתני מתני' שתי הלחם באין בטומאה, לאו בשתי הלחם הבאות בפני עצמן — כגון שלא היו להן כבשים, דאמרינן במנחות (דף מה:) דבאין בפני עצמן — ובהנהו לא קאמר מתני' דליתו בטומאה, אלא בבאו עם הכבשים. ומשום הכבשים הקריבין עמהן, ששחיטתן מקדשת את הלחם וזריקת דמם מתרת אותן, קאמר מתניתין דבאות בטומאה, משום דציץ מרצי עלייהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:10:1.english: And if you say - That which the Mishnah teaches [that] the Two Loaves come in [a state of] impurity is not [referring] to the Two Loaves that come by themselves — such as when they had no lambs, as we say in Menachot (45b) that they come by themselves — and regarding those, the Mishnah does not say that they come in impurity, rather [it refers to] when they came with the lambs. And it is because of the lambs that are sacrificed with them — whose slaughter sanctifies the bread and the sprinkling of whose blood permits them — [that] the Mishnah says that they come in impurity, because the frontplate appeases for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:11:1.english: [Ritual impurity] is permitted in [cases involving] the public - And we do not require the frontplate.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:1.hebrew: אחד זה ואחד זה - אחד כהן השורף את הפרה ואחד כהן גדול ביום הכפורים, שטעונין פרישה שבעת ימים:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:1.english: Both this [one] and that [one] - Both the priest who burns the [red] heifer and the High Priest on Yom Kippur, who require separation [for] seven days.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:2.hebrew: מכל חטאות - מכל אפרי הפרות שהיו במקדש, שאפר פרה של משה לא כלתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:2.english: From all the purification offerings - From all the ashes of the [red] heifers that were in the Temple, for the ashes of Moses' [red] heifer had not been exhausted.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:3.hebrew: כל שבעה - בפ"ק דיומא מפרש טעמא: בראשון לפרישתו — שמא היום שלישי לטומאתו, שמא היום ג' ימים שניטמא במת, וחששא בעלמא היא ומעלה. וכן שני — שמא שלישי, ושלישי — שמא שלישי, ואינך — מספקינן כל חד וחד בז' לטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:12:3.english: All seven [days] - In the first chapter of Yoma, [the Gemara] explains the reason: on the first [day] of his separation, [we sprinkle on him] lest today is the third [day] of his impurity — [meaning] perhaps today it is three days since he became impure through a corpse — and this is merely a concern and a stringency. And similarly [on the] second [day], perhaps [it is the] third [day]; and [on the] third [day], perhaps [it is the] third [day]; and [on] the remaining [days], we treat each and every one as possibly the seventh [day] of impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:13:1.hebrew: הזאה למה לי - הא קרבן דיום הכפורים דציבור הוא ודוחה טומאה, אלא ש"מ בקושי נדחית טומאה בקרבנות ובעי ריצוי ציץ. וכיון דלא מרצי אאכילות, לא מיתוקם שתי הלחם דמתניתין כר' יוסי, ואפילו סבירא ליה דבחדא סגיא, דהא אפילו חדא ליכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:13:1.english: Why do I need sprinkling - Behold, the offering of Yom Kippur is a communal [offering] and overrides ritual impurity; rather, learn from this [that] ritual impurity is overridden [only] with difficulty in [the case of] offerings, and it requires the appeasement of the frontplate. And since [the frontplate] does not appease for [the impurity of] foods, the Two Loaves of our Mishnah cannot be established in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, even if he holds that one [sprinkling] suffices, for behold, there is not even one.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:14:1.hebrew: שטרא מזכי לבי תרי הוא - בתמיה, כלומר: מי ראה שטר שמזכה את התובע ואת הנתבע? דקאמר רבי יוסי: רואה אני את דברי שניהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:14:1.english: [Is he] a document that awards to two [parties]? - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question, meaning: who has ever seen a document that awards [in favor of both] the claimant and the defendant? For Rabbi Yosei says, "I see [as correct] the words of both of them."

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:16:1.english: He said "it is reasonable" - He said [that] it is reasonable that they disagree in both [of them].

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:17:1.english: The essential verses - [The verse:] "And you shall offer your burnt-offerings."

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:17:2.hebrew: בזבחים כתיבי - ובמנחות לא כתיבי, ואצטריך לאשמעי' דאפ"ה פליגי במנחות:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:17:2.english: Are written with regard to [animal] offerings - And regarding meal-offerings they are not written, and it was necessary to teach us that even so, they disagree regarding meal-offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:1:1.hebrew: ביחיד - לכתחלה פסולה, ואם זרק הורצה. ומתני' בציבור, באין לכתחלה, דטומאת ציבור הוא בהיתר:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:1:1.english: With an individual - Ab initio it is invalid, and if [the priest] sprinkled [the blood], it is accepted. And [the] Mishnah [refers to] the public — they come ab initio, for impurity of the public is [offered] with permission.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:21:1.hebrew: ועוד - בציבור, ר' אליעזר הוא דמכשיר ולא ר' יהושע. בתמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:21:1.english: And furthermore - In [the case of] the public, is it Rabbi Eliezer who validates [it] and not Rabbi Yehoshua? [This is] a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:2:1.hebrew: לימא מתני' דלא כר' יוסי - דכיון דא"ר יוסי בעינן תרתי, כדמפרש ואזיל: מדקאמר רבי יוסי אין הציץ מרצה על אכילות, ש"מ כרבי יהושע סבירא ליה דבעי תרתי; ואשמעינן הכא דניטמא בשר, לא מהני ליה ציץ למהוי כי בשר קיים לזרוק את הדם. דאי לא בעי תרתי, ריצוי ציץ אאכילות למה לי? הא בלאו אכילות נמי מיתכשרא זריקת דם:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:2:1.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - For since Rabbi Yosei says we require both [meat and blood], as [the Gemara] goes on to explain: from the fact that Rabbi Yosei says the frontplate does not appease for portions eaten, learn from this that he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua, who requires both; and [our Mishnah] teaches us here that [when] the meat became impure, the frontplate is not effective for it to be [considered] like existing meat to sprinkle the blood. For if he did not require both, why would I need appeasement of the frontplate for portions eaten? Behold, even without portions eaten, the sprinkling of the blood is valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:4:1.hebrew: כרבי אליעזר ס"ל - דבחדא סגיא, ולקמן פריך: שתי הלחם אפילו חדא ליכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:4:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer he holds - that one suffices. And later [the Gemara] asks: [Regarding] the Two Loaves, there is not even one!

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:5:1.hebrew: למאי אין הציץ מרצה על אכילות - למאי מיבעי לן ריצוי ציץ דידהו? אלא על כרחיך, לרבי אליעזר, ריצוי דציץ דאכילות לאו לאכשורי זריקה מיבעי לן לאפוקי בעלים — דבלאו אכילות נמי מיתכשר — אלא לאכילות גופייהו מיבעי לן:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:5:1.english: With regard to what [halakha] does the frontplate not appease [God] for [the] eaten portions - For what [purpose] do we need the appeasement of the frontplate for them? Rather, perforce, according to Rabbi Eliezer, the appeasement of the frontplate for [the] eaten portions is not needed by us to validate the sprinkling [so as] to discharge the owners — for without [the] eaten portions it is also valid — rather, it is needed by us for the eaten portions themselves.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:1.hebrew: למיקבעינהו בפיגול - דקי"ל, אם יש פסול אחר בקרבן שחישב בו מחשבת פיגול, אינו נקבע בפיגול להתחייב כרת על אכילתו, דאמר מר: "ירצה" — כהרצאת כשר, כך הרצאת פיגול, במסכת מנחות (דף יו:):
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:1.english: To establish them as piggul - For we hold that if there is another disqualification in an offering in which one had an intention of piggul [to eat it beyond its allotted time], it is not established as piggul [so as] to incur karet [excision] for eating it; as the Master said [regarding the verse's expression] "it shall be accepted" [yirtzeh]: like the acceptance of a valid [offering], so is the acceptance of piggul, in Tractate Menachot (16b).

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:2.hebrew: ולאפוקי להאי בשר מידי מעילה - דבקדשי קדשים, זריקתן משוי בבשרן שעת היתר לכהנים, ותו לא קדשי ה' מיקרו, ונפקו מידי מעילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:2.english: And to exclude this meat from [the prohibition of] misuse of consecrated property - For in [the case of] offerings of the most sacred order, their [blood] sprinkling establishes for their meat a time of permissibility for the priests, and they are no longer called "consecrated property of the Lord," and they are excluded from [the prohibition of] misuse of consecrated property.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:3.hebrew: ומשוי לי' כי טהור - ואע"ג דאסור לאוכלו בטומאה, מיהו לכל שאר מילי הוי כי טהור, ומהניא ליה זריקה למיקבעיה בפיגול כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:6:3.english: And it renders it like pure [meat] - Even though it is forbidden to eat it in [a state of] impurity, nevertheless for all other matters it is like pure [meat], and the sprinkling [of the blood] is effective for it to establish it as piggul, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי סבר - נהי דזריקה כשירה היא להוציא את הבעלים ידי נדרן, דלא בעינן תרתי; מיהו להאי בשר לא מהני ציץ למהוי הך זריקה מהניא ליה למיקבעה בפיגול ולאפוקה מידי מעילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds - Granted that the sprinkling [of the blood] is valid to discharge the owners of their vow, for we do not require both [the blood and the meat]; however, the frontplate is not effective for this [impure] meat so that this sprinkling would be effective for it to establish it as piggul and to remove it from [the prohibition of] me'ilah.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:2.hebrew: בשלמא זבחים - דמתני' איכא עולין דמרצי ציץ עלייהו, ואיכא תרתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:2.english: Granted, animal offerings - [those] of the Mishnah: there are [parts that] ascend [the altar] upon which the frontplate effects acceptance, and there are two [components].

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:3.hebrew: עומר נמי דאיכא קומץ - דמרצי ציץ עליה, וחדא מיהא איכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:3.english: [The] omer, too, where there is a handful - For the frontplate effects acceptance for it, and there is at least one.

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:4.hebrew: ובלחם הפנים איכא בזיכין - שמתירין את הלחם כקומץ למנחה, דכתיב ביה (ויקרא כ״ד:ז׳) והיתה ללחם לאזכרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:4.english: And [with] the shewbread, there are bowls - which permit the bread like a handful [permits] a meal-offering, as it is written regarding it (Leviticus 24:7): "And it shall be for the bread as a memorial portion."

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:5.hebrew: בזיכים - לבונה של לחם הפנים, וכתיב בקומץ (שם ב) "והקטיר הכהן את אזכרתה". וציץ מרצי עלייהו, דהא עולים נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:8:5.english: Bowls [of frankincense] - [This refers to the] frankincense of the showbread; and it is written regarding the handful (ibid. 2), "And the priest shall burn its memorial portion." And the frontplate effects acceptance for them, for they go up [upon the altar].

Rashi on Pesachim 78a:9:1.hebrew: אלא שתי הלחם - דכולה אכילות, ור' יוסי אין הציץ מרצה על אכילות קאמר, מאי איכא למימר:
Rashi on Pesachim 78a:9:1.english: Rather, the two loaves - Since [they are] entirely [for] eating, and Rabbi Yosei says [that] the frontplate does not effect acceptance for eating, what is there to say?

Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:12:1.hebrew: מכלל דרבי יוסי כרבי יהושע ס"ל - תימה לרשב"א: מנא ליה הא? דילמא כר' אליעזר סבירא ליה, ואין הציץ מרצה על אכילות; נפקא מינה לשתי הלחם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:12:1.english: From [this] it follows that Rabbi Yosei holds like Rabbi Yehoshua - It is puzzling to Rashba: from where does [the Gemara] know this? Perhaps he holds like Rabbi Eliezer, and [that] the frontplate does not effect acceptance for eating; [and] the practical difference [would be] with regard to the Two Loaves:

Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:17:1.hebrew: והא עיקר קראי בזבחים כתיבי - תימה לר"י: לריש לקיש דאמר במנחות פרק קמא (דף ט.) שירים שחסרו בין קמיצה להקטרה אין מקטיר קומץ עליהן — אדרבה, קראי במנחות כתיבי! דבזבחים, כיון שנשתייר כזית בשר זורק את הדם, ומשמע התם דטעמיה מקרא דכתיב "המנחה". מיהו לרבי יוחנן דפליג עליה התם, אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:17:1.english: "Aren't the essential verses written with regard to animal offerings?" - This is puzzling to the R"i: according to Reish Lakish, who says in Menachot, in the first chapter (9a), [that if] the remainder [of a meal-offering] became diminished between the scooping [of the handful] and the burning [on the altar], one does not burn the handful on its behalf — on the contrary, the verses are written with regard to meal-offerings! For with regard to animal offerings, once an olive-bulk of meat remains, one sprinkles the blood, and it is implied there that his reason [regarding meal-offerings] is from a verse, as it is written: "the meal-offering." However, according to Rabbi Yochanan, who disagrees with him there, it works out well.

Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:1:1.hebrew: הא לא קשיא הא ביחיד והא בציבור - פי' בקונטרס דסבירא לן טומאה הותרה בציבור. וקשה, דה"ל למימר: "אלא קסבר רבי יהושע טומאה הותרה בציבור", כדמסיק לעיל דקסבר ציץ מרצה על אכילות. ועוד, היכי קאמר בסמוך: "נימא דלא כרבי יוסי דאמר אין הציץ מרצה על אכילות"? מהאי טעמא גופיה דטומאה הותרה בציבור דאוקימנא כרבי יהושע, אתי נמי כר' יוסי, כדקאמר נמי לבסוף. ונראה לר"י דלעולם סבירא ליה טומאה דחויה, אלא דסבירא ליה דהציץ מרצה על אכילות, וביחיד לכתחלה לא יזרוק מדרבנן, ו"פסולה" דקתני היינו לכתחלה; הלכך בציבור באין לכתחלה. ואם תאמר: ומאי איכא בין ציבור ליחיד, הואיל ומדאורייתא ביחיד נמי זורק לכתחלה? יש לומר: טומאת הגוף איכא בינייהו, דבציבור דחיא, ביחיד לא דחיא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78a:1:1.english: "This is not difficult: this [refers to] an individual, and this [refers to] the public" - Rashi explained that we hold [that] impurity is permitted for the public. And this is difficult, for [the Gemara] should have said, "Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua holds [that] impurity is permitted for the public," just as it concludes above that he holds the tzitz effects acceptance for eating. And furthermore, how does [the Gemara] say shortly below, "Shall we say [it is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who says the tzitz does not effect acceptance for eating"? By this very same reason — that impurity is permitted for the public — by which we established [it] in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, it also accords with Rabbi Yosei, just as [the Gemara] indeed says at the end. And it appears to the Ri that in fact he holds impurity is [merely] overridden, rather he holds that the tzitz effects acceptance for eating, and for an individual one may not sprinkle [the blood] ab initio by rabbinic decree, and "invalid" that [the baraita] teaches means ab initio; therefore, for the public they come [and offer it] ab initio. And if you will say: What [difference] is there between the public and an individual, since by Torah law for an individual too one may sprinkle ab initio? One can say: Impurity of the body is [the difference] between them, for in the case of the public it is overridden, whereas in the case of an individual it is not overridden.
